pages.text: $(item)Empty Pages$() are made from paper and await a command. $(item)Symbol Pages$() are words with teeth: terrain, weather, color, sun, hunger, mercy. $(item)Lost Pages$() are sealed scraps found in stronghold libraries and Age structures; use one to reveal a weighted random symbol.

$(item)Leather$() alone in the $(thing)Book Binder$() yields a blank $(item)Descriptive Book$(). Treat it as an unwoken door. Feed it symbols one by one until its sentence resembles the world you dare to visit.

$(item)Leather$() with an $(item)Empty Page$() makes an unlinked $(item)Linking Book$(). Use it once to bind your exact dimension, position, standing height, pitch, and nearest cardinal facing. Loose symbols nearby are spared, for a return path should not devour the map that made the journey.

The blue field in the binder is no ornament. There you name the sleeping Age. The craft trims ugly marks and repeated names, not from vanity, but to keep one world's door from opening into another's bones.

When you are ready to work with more care, move to the $(thing)Writing Desk$(). There a notebook may be copied cleanly into a descriptive book, and a linked Age may be retitled without reopening the binder's rough first work.

Once a descriptive book is linked, its first leaf becomes a survey and naming page. There you may retitle the Age in a steadier hand. In survival, a true crossing leaves behind an anchored volume: the very book, resting where you departed, unwilling to fade. In creative, it remains in hand.

That first leaf now carries more than words. A linked descriptive book shows a small field-card of the Age when one has been taken, and a linking book does the same for its bound destination. If the picture seems stale, use the refresh mark and let the binding take a new measure.

Even when cast to the ground by hand, a $(thing)linked$() descriptive book dislikes becoming common litter. It settles into that same anchored form instead of lying loose. Touch or use an anchor to recover it safely. Breaking one releases an ordinary item with a brief two-second grace period before it may anchor again.
